summary: Shuntaro Matsuyama was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1953). He served as a professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design (~1972–1996) and held posts at Kokugakuin and Tama Art universities.

Shunzo Onoda is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his D.Lit. at Bukkyo University in 1993. His academic career includes serving as an associate professor (attested 1996) and professor (attested 2005) at Bukkyo University.

Shuyu Kanaoka was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1954). He held posts at Toyo University as assistant professor (~1959–1965) and professor (~1965–1992), and at Ryukoku University (attested 1962).

Shōkin Furuta was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Shimane University and taught Kotatsu Fujita. He was director of Matsugaoka Bunko (~1984–2001) and held posts attested in 1998 at Hokkaido University and Nihon University.
Shōkō Kabutogi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1933–1936). He later served as a professor at Rissho University from approximately 1960 to 1982.
Shūei Tsuboi was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at Bukkyo University, with his tenure attested in 1963 and 1972.

Shūichi Katō studied at the University of Tokyo (~1940–1943), working in Japanology and philosophy. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, University of British Columbia, Free University of Berlin, Sophia University, Yale University, and Ritsumeikan University (~1993–2008).

Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under J. Sitaramamma. He also studied under ten traditional teachers, including U Kundala, U Sajjanasāra, and U Sāsana.

Sibani Dasgupta is an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka and under Rajendra Chandra Hazra. She completed a doctorate degree at the University of Calcutta by 1954 under the supervision of Sushil Kumar De.

Sibraj Chetry is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Sibnath Sarma, D. K. Chakravarty, N. Sharma, Girish Sarma, and M. Boruah. In 2012, he was attested as Lecturer of Philosophy at North Lakhimpur College.

Siegfried Goldschmidt was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1864, at the University of Tübingen in 1867, and under Rudolf von Roth (~1866–1869). He later taught Heinrich Zimmer.

Siegfried Lienhard was an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1943–1949) and taught Leif Asplund. He held posts at the University of Kiel (~1962–1967) and Stockholm University, where he was attested as professor in 1991.

Siglinde Dietz is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned her PhD at the University of Bonn under Michael Hahn in 1980. She held a post at the University of Göttingen (attested 1990) and taught Ryutaro Tsuchida.
Signe Howell was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford (~1974–1980). She held a post at the University of Oslo from approximately 1987 to 2012 and taught Heidi Fjeld.

Sik Fanin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed a PhD at Lancaster University by 2008. She held an instructional advisor post attested in 2013 at the University of Hong Kong.

Silvio Vita studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton University, specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He was director of the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~2000–2015) and held professorial posts at several Italian universities.
Simo Parpola is a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He served as Professor of Assyriology at the University of Helsinki from approximately 1979 to 2009.

Simon P. James is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who taught Colette Sciberras. He held posts at Durham University as a philosophy tutor (attested 2001) and philosophy lecturer (attested 2013–2014).
Singhathon Narāsabho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD from Visva-Bharati University, studying under doctoral supervisor Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti (attested 1971).

Siniruddha Dash is an Indologist and linguist who served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras (2000–2014, attested 2022). He was also attested as director at the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore, in 2013.
